CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

AGENTS.md predates this file and holds the repository’s own style, testing and pull request guidelines for any agent. It overlaps the shared files on commands, roxygen and commit style; where they differ, this file and the shared files win for Claude Code. Deviations are stated as such below.

What this is

An R client for the OpenLineage specification: build and validate run events, serialize them to JSON with the wire field names, and deliver them through a transport. The OpenLineage Python client is the behavioural reference, but its non-R APIs are not copied. Event models stay separate from serialization, configuration and transport code.

Deviation from the zero-dependency rule: runtime dependencies are cli (conditions), httr2 (HTTP), jsonlite (JSON), R6 (the stateful client and transports), S7 (models and validation) and uuid (run IDs). Justify any new one.

There is no design or roadmap document and no .agents/ directory. The exported docs, vignettes/openlineage-lifecycle.Rmd, the golden fixtures and the tests are the contract.

Current state

On CRAN as 0.1.0 (published 2026-07-30). main is the development version, 0.1.0.9000, with no changes yet under its NEWS.md heading. It targets OpenLineage schema 2.0.2 (OPENLINEAGE_SCHEMA_VERSION).

Implemented: S7 models for run states, runs, jobs, datasets and run events; typed core facets (nominal time, parent run, error message, processing engine, schema, data source, SQL, source code location, job type, input and output statistics, tags) and generic facets; deterministic JSON serialization; UUID and event-time helpers; console, no-op and accumulating local transports; a synchronous HTTP transport; and the R6 OpenLineageClient. Not implemented: asynchronous or batched delivery, and transports other than HTTP (for example Kafka or file).

Gaps from the shared rules, as of 2026-11-11:

  • R-CMD-check.yaml is the hand-rolled r-lib template, not a call to pedrobtz/r-actions, so it does not count as the pre-submission check. Issue #8 tracks the move. coverage.yaml calls r-actions’ coverage.yml at @v1, not at a commit pin, although it holds a write token.
  • No cran-release.yaml; the .9000 bump was a hand-made pull request.
  • No .agents/assurance.md.
  • cran-comments.md still lists a local macOS check as its test environment, not CI legs.

Commands

The shared commands apply. Specific to this package:

Rscript -e 'pkgdown::check_pkgdown()'            # reference index is complete

Architecture

One focused file per concern under R/, each mirrored by tests/testthat/test-<name>.R.

  • Models (R/models.R). S7 classes RunState, Run, Job, Dataset, InputDataset, OutputDataset and RunEvent, with validators. R/zzz.R calls S7::methods_register() in .onLoad().
  • Facets (R/ol-facets.R). Abstract S7 bases (.OpenLineageFacet, .RunFacet, .JobFacet, .DatasetFacet, .InputDatasetFacet, .OutputDatasetFacet, .GenericFacet), the typed facets, tags, and the wire-name tables .ol_facet_wire_maps and .ol_record_wire_maps.
  • Serialization (R/serialization.R). as_openlineage_list() walks a model to named lists through .ol_to_wire(), applying wire names, dropping NULL properties and unwrapping RunState. to_openlineage_json() calls jsonlite::toJSON() with auto_unbox = TRUE and digits = NA.
  • Transports (R/transports.R, R/z-http-transport.R). The internal R6 base .OpenLineageTransport and the local transports, then HttpTransport, which inherits from it. The z- prefix makes the HTTP file collate after R/transports.R, since R6 resolves inherit when the file is sourced.
  • Client (R/client.R). OpenLineageClient picks its transport: a no-op one if disabled (or OPENLINEAGE_DISABLED=true), the injected transport if given, HTTP if url or OPENLINEAGE_URL is set, and the console otherwise. OPENLINEAGE_ENDPOINT and OPENLINEAGE_API_KEY fill arguments left unset.
  • Shared helpers. R/validation.R (.ol_validate_*(), .ol_normalize_*()), R/conditions.R (.ol_abort()), R/constants.R (schema version, URLs, producer), R/run-id.R and R/event-time.R.

Internal objects carry the .ol_ prefix (or .OpenLineage for internal classes); exported names follow OpenLineage’s own class names (RunEvent, HttpTransport), so CamelCase there is deliberate. The code uses the base pipe (|>).

Deviation: README.md is the source; there is no README.Rmd.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • Wire names exist only at the serialization boundary. R-facing properties are snake_case (event_time, run_id, schema_url); .ol_model_fields() and the wire maps translate them to eventTime, runId, schemaURL, _producer. A new facet needs an entry in .ol_facet_wire_maps, or serialization fails with “No wire mapping is registered”.
  • Output must match the Python client. tests/testthat/fixtures/ holds JSON produced by the Python client at a recorded upstream commit (see its README.md), and test-golden-fixtures.R compares against them. A change in key names, NULL omission or number formatting breaks that parity.
  • Every error is an openlineage_error. Conditions carry openlineage_validation_error, openlineage_config_error or openlineage_transport_error as well. Most go through .ol_abort(); R/client.R and R/z-http-transport.R build some by hand with call = NULL. HTTP failures carry status_code.
  • Credentials are never printed. HttpTransport passes every custom header to httr2::req_headers() with .redact, and the client and transport print() methods show only the transport class, the endpoint and the kind of authentication. An API key together with a custom Authorization header is an error.
  • Retry policy. Only HTTP 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504 and httr2 connection failures are retried, at most max_retries times after the first attempt. The delay honours Retry-After (capped at 60 s), otherwise backs off as 2^(n - 1) seconds capped at 30. 401 and 403 are never retried. .ol_http_retry_sleep() is the one place that sleeps, so tests can replace it.
  • verify_tls = FALSE warns with openlineage_insecure_tls_warning.
  • transport = excludes HTTP arguments. Passing it with url, api_key or any non-default HTTP argument is a config error, and so are HTTP settings without a URL.
  • new_event_time() emits UTC with exactly three fractional digits (2026-01-02T03:04:05.000Z), truncating rather than rounding.

Testing

  • The suite is fully offline and needs no OpenLineage server. HTTP is tested with httr2::local_mocked_responses(), which also asserts the request’s endpoint, headers, body and retries. A test against a local stub server must be opt-in.
  • tests/testthat/helper-events.R gives fixture_run_id() and fixture_event_time(), deterministic inputs for events.
  • tests/testthat/helper-json.R gives read_json_fixture() and expect_json_semantically_equal(), which compares parsed JSON with object keys sorted. Compare parsed JSON unless formatting itself is under test.
  • The golden fixtures are the conformance oracle, generated with the Python client (tests/testthat/fixtures/README.md records the commit and version). No other external corpus is used.
  • Condition wording is pinned in snapshots under tests/testthat/_snaps/.

Continuous integration

  • R-CMD-check.yaml: the r-lib template matrix, macOS and Windows release and Ubuntu devel, release and oldrel-1, built with --compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf. No CRAN-like containers and no nosuggests leg (see Current state).
  • coverage.yaml: calls r-actions’ coverage.yml@v1; .github/badges/coverage.svg is the badge.
  • pkgdown.yaml: the r-lib template, deploying to gh-pages with clean: false.
